---
title: What you can change
description: The exact fields a verified owner may edit, the ones they may not, and why the line falls where it does.
---

Once a claim is approved, you can propose changes to your listing. "Propose" is the
operative word: every change is reviewed before it is published.

The line is drawn at **anything a reader would use to compare tools against each other.**

## Yours to propose

| Field               | Notes                                                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Name**            |                                                                       |
| **Tagline**         | One line, shown under the name                                        |
| **Summary**         | Short description used in listings and cards                          |
| **Website**         |                                                                       |
| **Pricing page**    | The most useful field here — it is what our price checks read         |
| **Documentation**   |                                                                       |
| **Logo URL**        | See [logos and screenshots](/docs/vendors/logos-and-screenshots)      |
| **From the vendor** | Your own copy, published in its own labelled block                    |
| **Facets**          | Media, deployment, method, compliance, platform, capability, audience |

**"From the vendor"** is a real block on your listing, marked as yours. It is the place to
say what you want said in your own words. What it does not do is count toward the
several-hundred-word minimum a listing must clear — that has to be our own writing, or the
catalog stops being a comparison.

**Facets travel as a whole list.** You propose the complete set rather than adding or
removing one at a time, and the set is reviewed together. They are the one editable thing a
reader filters on, so they get the same review as everything else.

## Not yours, at any status

| Field                                      | Why                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Slug**                                   | It is a published URL — in the sitemap, in inbound links, with no redirect story                |
| **Status**                                 | Draft, published, archived is a lifecycle transition, not an edit                               |
| **Our description**                        | The comparison itself. See above                                                                |
| **Strengths and limitations**              | Our editorial judgement                                                                         |
| **Editor notes**                           | Internal                                                                                        |
| **Prices**                                 | Proposals only — see [correcting a price](/docs/vendors/correcting-a-price)                     |
| **Plans and their limits**                 | Same route                                                                                      |
| **Benchmark scores**                       | Measured, not stated. You can [submit runs](/docs/benchmarks/submitting-results); we score them |
| **Sort order, first-party flag**           | Placement is not for sale, and if a tool is ours the listing says so                            |
| **Last verified / price freshness stamps** | Set by the price checking process. Typing them by hand would make the staleness signal a lie    |

## Why review at all

Because the alternative does not work. A catalog whose entries are written by the vendors
being compared is a directory of marketing copy, and a buyer can get that from the vendors
directly. The review is the product.

It is not adversarial. Most proposals are corrections to things we got wrong or that
changed, and those go through quickly.
